This page lists every known error in the published reviews, with the date it was found and what was changed. Corrections are inserted into the affected review as dated notes; the original sentence is left in place so readers can see what was wrong. The round-two Claude syntheses also carry a Verification notes section in which the overseer model tagged each checked sub-review claim as CONFIRMED, CORRECTED or COULD NOT CHECK; across the 13 round-two papers, 14 of 264 checked claims were corrected at that stage. Those in-pipeline corrections are visible in each synthesis and are not repeated here.

## Per-paper notes

- [Xu, Flanagan & Quintero](papers/P15_xu/index.qmd) (EEPA): The PDF reviewed was typeset 2026-07-17, before the corrigendum published 2026-08-07 (doi 10.3102/01623737261473601). The corrigendum adds an author acknowledgment and changes no results.
- [Cleveland & Lukes](papers/P22_cleveland/index.qmd) (EEPA): As of 2026-09-25, Crossref lists no correction or corrigendum for this article. The review's central finding about Figure 3 should be re-checked against the journal's current version before being relied on.
- [Cleveland & Lukes](papers/P22_cleveland/index.qmd) (EEPA): The online supplement, obtained 2026-09-25, contains the numbers behind the intended figure: Supplemental Table A4, Panel A, reports district per-pupil revenue by HOLC grade for 1989–90, 1999–00, 2009–10 and 2017–18, cell for cell identical to Table 4 of the authors' 2021 working paper (Annenberg EdWorkingPaper 21-363). Neither the article nor the supplement contains a correctly rendered version of Figure 3; the working paper's Figure 4 is the only dollar-scale rendering of these series in the public record. On the supplement's numbers, the A–D gap in local revenue grows from \$3,592 to \$5,874 over the period, the state-aid offset grows from −\$1,575 to −\$3,854, federal revenue roughly doubles for every grade in 2009–10 and falls back by 2017–18, and the A–D gap in total revenue falls from \$1,688 (p<.01) to \$1,291 (not significant). Separately, the trend figures quoted in the article's text for school racial composition (a Black-share gap shrinking from 13.4 to 10.3 points, a White-share gap of about 35 points, diversity gaps beyond 0.08) appear verbatim in the working paper's text and do not match Supplemental Table A4, Panel B, where the A–D Black-share gap is 0.09 to 0.10 in every year, the White-share gap 0.26 to 0.29, and the largest diversity gap 0.06. Supplemental Table A7 shows the school-level achievement and composition gradients holding with controls for family income, building age and percent Black.
- [Holzman, Han, Lewis et al.](papers/P03_holzman/index.qmd) (AERA Open): The openICPSR deposit (10.3886/E249905V1, read 2026-09-26) confirms what both reviews infer from the article: no pooled model exists. RaceNativityLabor_MainResults.do estimates Tables 3–4 in a loop over race groups, and no script contains a race × linkage term or any cross-group test (no suest, test, lincom, nlcom or margins). Approximate z-tests from the reported standard errors put the Black–White and Hispanic–White differences in Linkage × Match at z = 2.3 and 2.9 for earnings, so the abstract's "benefit more" claim survives for earnings among Black and Hispanic workers and not for unemployment. The same deposit shows Appendix Table A1 follows the stated ratio rule (see the correction on the Claude review).
- [Holtz](papers/P06_holtz/index.qmd) (AERA Open): The ICPSR deposit (study 308283, read 2026-09-26) settles what Table 2 is. Its README states that tract-level income and immigrant density were joined to campuses "for the descriptive table analysis" and that county ACS processing served the choropleth maps only, so Table 2's bins are census tracts mislabeled as counties; relabelling them reconciles every sum, and the note (69 of 74 TWDL hot spots in El Paso County) and Figure 3 are right. The TEA program file is not deposited, so the table cannot be recounted. Separately, the abstract's conclusions were carried nearly verbatim from the author's 2023 Texas A&M dissertation, which ran the hot-spot analysis on raw enrollment (hot spots in San Antonio, Austin and El Paso); the article re-ran it on enrollment ratios, which moved the TWDL hot spots to El Paso County, and kept the conclusions.
- [Odle, Duke & Dunens](papers/P07_odle/index.qmd) (AERA Open): The openICPSR deposit (248577, read 2026-09-26) settles the 38% Pell share that appears only in prose: line 664 of HPP_Analysis.Rmd computes it as the mean of IPEDS percent Pell over the pooled 2015–2019 analytic sample (1,462 institution-years). The same file shows the criterion-3 model is trained on 2015–2018 and predicts 2019, so the prediction is out of sample.
- [Gilmour, Bartanen, Bettini et al.](papers/P11_gilmour/index.qmd) (AERJ): The online supplement, read 2026-09-26, bears on the Discussion's "turnover of nearly half the workforce (which we found in one state and in some locations in other states)." Charter-school total turnover in the supplement reaches 46–56% (Indiana 55.6%, Washington 55.7%, Texas 51.6%, Massachusetts 46.3%), which supports the "some locations" clause. The "one state" clause traces only to a single-year Texas figure (2022–23, 47.4%) in the OSF and working-paper over-time table, which appears in neither the article nor the supplement and which the posted code suggests double-counts switchers. The reviews' statement that the article's highest statewide figure is 35.9% is correct.
- [Acris, Ganimian, King & Marple-Cantrell](papers/P23_acris/index.qmd) (EEPA): The external record, read 2026-09-26, contains cost data the article does not: the program's endline report has a cost-effectiveness annex (pp. 131–132) giving about \$90 per student, about \$9,000 per school (about \$6,000 marginal) and about \$290 per standard deviation of knowledge gain, which the authors compare with \$95.60 per SD for Kenyan textbooks. The reviews' statements that the article reports no cost data are correct; the "scalable model" claim can be read against these figures.
- [Polikoff, Rowley, Silver et al.](papers/P29_polikoff/index.qmd) (ER): The UAS 567 methodology documentation, read 2026-09-26, explains the half sample in Models 9–13 of Table 3 (N = 1,727–1,827 against 3,892): the attitude items were on Form A, administered to a random half of respondents. The article never says so. The same documentation reconciles the response rate and the regression Ns (see the corrections on both reviews).

To report an error, open an issue in the site's GitHub repository or use the discussion thread on the paper's page.
